\HLASourcePage{18}{17}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
The formal definition of the M\&S HLA comprises three main components: the HLA framework and rules
specification (found in IEEE Std 1516\texttrademark-2025), the HLA federate interface specification (found in this
document), and the HLA object model template (OMT) (found in IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025). This standard,
IEEE Std 1516.1-2025, provides a complete description of the essential elements of the second component
of the HLA, the interface specification.\textsuperscript{\fontsize{7.98pt}{8pt}\selectfont 8}

The HLA is an integrated architecture that has been developed to provide a common architecture for M\&S.
The HLA requires that interfederate communications use a standard application programmer's interface
(API). This specification defines the standard services and interfaces to be used by the federates in order to
support efficient information exchange when participating in a distributed federation execution.
Additionally, the capability for reuse of individual federates that adhere to these standard services and
interfaces is increased.

This document provides a specification for the HLA functional interfaces between federates and the runtime
infrastructure (RTI). The RTI provides services to federates in a way that is analogous to how a distributed
operating system provides services to applications. These interfaces are arranged into seven basic service
groups, and an eighth group of support services, as follows:

\begin{hlaalphlist}
 \item Federation management
 \item Declaration management (DM)
 \item Object management
 \item Ownership management
 \item Time management
 \item Data distribution management (DMM)
 \item Support services
\end{hlaalphlist}

The eight service groups describe the interface between the federates and the RTI and between the federates
and the software services provided by the RTI for use by HLA federates. The RTI requires a set of services
from the federate that are referred to as ``RTI-initiated'' and are denoted with a \textdagger{} (printer's dagger) after the
service name.

\begingroup\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\vspace{0.2pt}
\HLAAnchor{clause:1.4.1}\pdfbookmark[2]{1.4.1 HLA federation object model (FOM) framework}{bookmark:clause:1.4.1}\HLASubsubclause{1.4.1 HLA federation object model (FOM) framework}
\vspace{9.4pt}
\endgroup

A concise and rigorous description of the object model framework is essential to the specification of the
interface between federates and the RTI and of the HLA services. The rules and terminology used to
describe a FOM are described in IEEE Std 1516.2-2025. A simulation object model (SOM) describes salient
characteristics of a federate to aid in its reuse and other activities focused on the details of its internal
operation. As such, a SOM is not the concern of the RTI and its services. A FOM, on the other hand, deals
with interfederate issues and is relevant to the use of the RTI. FOMs describe the set of object classes and
interaction classes chosen for a planned federation along with the attributes of the object classes and
parameters of the interaction classes.

Every HLA object instance is an instance of an object class found in the FOM. Object classes are chosen by
the object model designer to facilitate an appropriate organizational scheme. Each object class has a set of
attributes associated with it. An attribute is a distinct, identifiable portion of the object's state. In this
discussion, ``attribute designator'' refers to the attribute, and ``attribute value'' refers to its contents. From the
federation perspective, the set of all attribute values for an object instance shall completely define the state
of that instance. Federates may associate additional state information with an object instance that is not
communicated between federates, but this action is outside the purview of the HLA FOM.

\vspace{0.4pt}
\HLACompactFootnote{8}{Information on references can be found in Clause 2.}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{19}{18}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{69.79}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Federates use the state of the object instances as one of the primary means of communication. At any point\linebreak
 during a federation execution, at most one federate or the RTI shall have the privilege to update the value of\linebreak
 a given object instance attribute. A joined federate that has the privilege to update values for an instance\linebreak
 attribute is said to own that instance attribute. There are specific (MOM) instance attributes that are owned\linebreak
 by the RTI. In some cases, an instance attribute may be unowned, neither owned by a federate nor the RTI.\linebreak
 The Ownership Management services allow joined federates to gain ownership of unowned instance\linebreak
 attributes, exchange ownership of instance attributes, or release ownership of instance attributes (possibly to\linebreak
 become unowned). The federate provides instance attribute values to the other federates in the federation\linebreak
 execution via Object Management services. The federate providing the instance attribute values is said to be\linebreak
 updating that instance attribute. Federates receiving those values are said to be reflecting that instance\linebreak
 attribute.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{213.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Each object instance shall have a designator. The value of an object instance designator shall be unique for\linebreak
 each federation execution. Object instance designators shall be dynamically generated by the RTI.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{249.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The FOM framework also allows for interaction classes for each object model. The types of interactions\linebreak
 possible and their parameters are specified within the FOM.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{285.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 A \textbf{federation} is the combination of a particular FOM, a particular set of federates, and the HLA services. A\linebreak
 federation is designed for a specific purpose using a commonly understood FOM and a set of federates that\linebreak
 may associate their individual semantics with that object model. A federation execution is an instance of the\linebreak
 \emph{Create Federation Execution} service invocation and entails executing the federation with a specific FOM\linebreak
 and RTI and using various execution details.%
 }

 \HLAAnchor{clause:1.5}
 \pdfbookmark[1]{1.5 General nomenclature and conventions}{bookmark:clause:1.5}
 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{363.38}{300}{\sffamily\bfseries\raggedright}{10.98}{13}{%
 1.5 General nomenclature and conventions%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{388.81}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 There are various entities (e.g., object classes, attributes, interaction classes, parameters, dimensions,\linebreak
 regions, federates, object instances) referenced in this document that may have the following different\linebreak
 views:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{430.80}{432}{6}{%
 \item Name: textual or for communication between federates.
 \item Handle: capable of being manipulated by a computer or for communication between a federate and\linebreak
 the RTI. A handle is originated by the RTI, federation execution-wide unique, and unpredictable.\linebreak
 The handle for a class attribute that is inherited shall be the same as the handle that is assigned to the\linebreak
 class attribute in the object class in which it is declared. The handle for a parameter that is inherited\linebreak
 shall be the same as the handle that is assigned to the parameter in the interaction class in which it is\linebreak
 declared.
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{532.80}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The following types of names shall be case-sensitive:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{548.82}{432}{3}{%
 \item Federation execution
 \item Federate
 \item Object class
 \item Attribute
 \item Object instance
 \item Interaction class
 \item Parameter
 \item Order
 \item Transportation type
 \item Dimension
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{20}{19}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{69.79}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The arguments to the services described in this document will use different views of the entities depending\linebreak
 on a particular RTI implementation. For clarity, the first 11 clauses of this document refer to only a generic\linebreak
 view, known as a ``designator,'' when referring to these entities, and the API annexes refer to the actual\linebreak
 implementation-specific arguments. Clause 12 ties the two concepts together.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{129.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Some of the arguments to the services described in this document are in the form of a group that represents\linebreak
 some association. These groupings can take several forms (depending on the requirements of the respective\linebreak
 service), each of which is described below. The groupings may be implemented slightly differently in each\linebreak
 API, but all implementations shall support the same semantics. These groupings are pairs, sets, collections,\linebreak
 constrained sets of pairs, and collections of pairs. Collections are sets that permit duplication of elements.\linebreak
 They are used in cases in which duplication is unlikely and not really an error. As such, using a collection\linebreak
 rather than a set retains the same effects, but without the expensive checks to eliminate duplicates that using\linebreak
 a set would require. In these cases, it is preferred not to penalize the majority of users with the less efficient\linebreak
 set just to catch errors that are anticipated to be infrequent.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{249.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The following data are needed for the implementation of a running RTI and federation executions:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{267.78}{432}{0}{%
 \item FOM Document Data (FDD): FOM information (e.g., class, attribute, parameter names) used by the\linebreak
 RTI at runtime. Each federation execution needs FDD. FDD is provided to the RTI starting with the\linebreak
 Management Object Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM) and FOM modules specified\linebreak
 in the \emph{Create Federation Execution} service invocation. FDD will also be provided by the MIM that\linebreak
 is automatically provided by the RTI or optionally provided in the \emph{Create Federation Execution}\linebreak
 service invocation. Additional FDD may be provided as joining federates specify additional FOM\linebreak
 modules.
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{363.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The following data may be needed for the implementation of a running RTI and federation executions:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{381.78}{432}{0}{%
 \item RTI initialization data (RID): RTI vendor-specific information needed to run an RTI. If required,\linebreak
 RID are supplied when an RTI is initialized.
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{417.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 For all joined federate-initiated services in this specification (except 4.2, 4.5, 4.6, and 4.11), an implied\linebreak
 supplied argument is a joined federate's conjointment with a federation execution. For all RTI-initiated\linebreak
 services, an implied supplied argument is also a joined federate's connection to a federation execution. The\linebreak
 manner in which these arguments are actually provided to the services is dependent on the RTI\linebreak
 implementation and the particular API programming language; therefore, it is not shown in the service\linebreak
 descriptions. Also, for the RTI-initiated services, some implicit preconditions are not stated explicitly\linebreak
 because the RTI is assumed to be well behaved. For many RTI-initiated services, the ``Federate is joined''\linebreak
 precondition presumes the ``Federate is connected'' precondition.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{525.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 As mentioned earlier, all RTI-initiated services are denoted with a \textdagger{} (printer's dagger) after the service\linebreak
 name.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{561.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 If an RTI-invoked service is not the result of a joined federate-invoked service, but the RTI-invoked service\linebreak
 has a user-supplied tag as a mandatory argument, the user-supplied tag shall be present in the service\linebreak
 invocation but empty. For example, in the Java API, the tag shall be an empty (zero-length) array. Examples\linebreak
 of RTI-invoked services with empty user-supplied tags are Provide Attribute Value Update (via Auto\linebreak
 Provide switch), Request Attribute Ownership (via Unconditional Divest resign directive), and MOM\linebreak
 HLAmanager.HLAfederate.HLAreport interactions.%
 }

 \HLAAnchor{clause:1.6}
 \pdfbookmark[1]{1.6 Organization of this document}{bookmark:clause:1.6}
 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{651.38}{250}{\sffamily\bfseries\raggedright}{10.98}{13}{%
 1.6 Organization of this document%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{676.81}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 The seven HLA service groups are specified in Clause 4 through Clause 10. Each service is described using\linebreak
 several components:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{706.81}{432}{0}{%
 \item Name and description: service name and narrative describing the functionality of the service.
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{21}{20}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{69.79}{432}{6}{%
 \item Supplied arguments: arguments supplied to the service
 \item Returned arguments: arguments returned by the service.
 \item Preconditions: conditions that shall exist for the service to execute correctly.
 \item Postconditions: conditions that shall exist once the service has executed correctly.
 \item Exceptions: notifications of any irregularity that may occur during service invocation. Wherever\linebreak
 possible (excepting situations like RTI internal error), exceptions are side-effect free. Exceptions are\linebreak
 listed in order of increasing precedence. That is, if the conditions for more than one exception are\linebreak
 met simultaneous, the RTI shall throw whichever of those exceptions comes later in the exception\linebreak
 list.
 \item Reference state charts: reference to state chart(s) that are germane to the service.
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{231.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 After the clauses describing each of the service groups are a clause describing the MOM and then a clause\linebreak
 that ties the service narratives with the APIs.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{267.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Annex A through Annex D contain HLA APIs for the following languages:%
 }

 \HLAFixedDashList{90}{285.78}{432}{6}{%
 \item Java
 \item C++
 \item Federate Protocol
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{345.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Annex E contains additional rationale for elements in the main body of this standard.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{369.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Annex F contains the FDD XML Schema.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{393.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Annex G contains the MIM.%
 }

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{417.78}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 Annex H and Annex I contain a list of figures and bibliography, respectively.%
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{24}{23}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLADefinitionAt{69.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{available-directed-interactions}\HLADefinitionTerm{available directed interactions}: The set of directed interaction classes of an object class in union with the\linebreak
 set of inherited directed interactions of that object class.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{105.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{available-parameters}\HLADefinitionTerm{available parameters}: The set of declared parameters of an interaction class in union with the set of\linebreak
 inherited parameters of that interaction class.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{141.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{base-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{base object model (BOM)}: A piece-part of a conceptual model, simulation object model (SOM), or\linebreak
 federation object model (FOM) that can be used as a building block in the development and/or extension of\linebreak
 a simulation or federation.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{189.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{best-effort}\HLADefinitionTerm{best effort}: A transportation type that does not provide any guarantee regarding delivery (messages may be\linebreak
 out of order, duplicate, or dropped).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{225.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{candidate-discovery-class}\HLADefinitionTerm{candidate discovery class}: The registered class of an object instance, if subscribed. If the registered class of\linebreak
 an object instance is not subscribed, the closest superclass of the registered class of the object instance to\linebreak
 which the joined federate is subscribed. Candidate discovery class pertains to object instances only.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{273.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{candidate-received-class}\HLADefinitionTerm{candidate received class}: The sent class of an interaction, if subscribed. If the sent class of an interaction is\linebreak
 not subscribed, the closest superclass of the sent class of the interaction to which the joined federate is\linebreak
 subscribed. Candidate received class pertains to interactions and directed interactions only.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{321.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{class}\HLADefinitionTerm{class}: A description of a group of items with similar properties, common behavior, common relationships,\linebreak
 and common semantics.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{357.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{class-attribute}\HLADefinitionTerm{class attribute}: A named characteristic of an object class denoted by a pair composed of an object class\linebreak
 designator and an attribute designator.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{393.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{class-directed-interaction}\HLADefinitionTerm{class directed interaction}: A named characteristic of an object class denoted by a pair composed of an\linebreak
 object class designator and an interaction class designator. The characteristic is the capability to have\linebreak
 interactions directed to instances of the object class or its subclasses.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{441.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{class-hierarchy}\HLADefinitionTerm{class hierarchy}: A specification of a class-subclass or ``is-a'' relationship between classes in a given\linebreak
 domain.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{477.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{coadunate}\HLADefinitionTerm{coadunate}: To attach an object instance handle and an object instance name to an object instance. The\linebreak
 object instance name can be provided specifically by the federate or implicitly by the runtime infrastructure\linebreak
 (RTI).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{525.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{collection}\HLADefinitionTerm{collection}: A group of elements in which an element may occur multiple times (this definition corresponds\linebreak
 to the mathematical notion of a bag).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{561.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{collection-of-pairs}\HLADefinitionTerm{collection of pairs}: A group of pairs in which multiple pairs may have the same first component and a given\linebreak
 pair may occur multiple times.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{597.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{compliant-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{compliant object model}: A High Level Architecture (HLA) federation object model (FOM) or simulation\linebreak
 object model (SOM) that fully conforms with all of the rules and constraints specified in object model\linebreak
 template (OMT).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{645.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{connection-fault}\HLADefinitionTerm{connection fault}: In the Federate Protocol, when the connection between the RTI and a federate becomes\linebreak
 inviable due to a broken socket connection or either the federate or the RTI exceeding the timeout interval.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{681.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{constrained-set-of-pairs}\HLADefinitionTerm{constrained set of pairs}: A group of pairs in which no two pairs have the same first component (this\linebreak
 definition corresponds to the mathematical notion of a function). An example would be a group of instance\linebreak
 attribute and value pairs; each instance attribute may have at most one value associated with it.%
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{25}{24}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLADefinitionAt{69.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{corresponding-class-attribute-of-an-instance-attribute}\HLADefinitionTerm{corresponding class attribute of an instance attribute}: The class attribute that, from the perspective of a\linebreak
 given joined federate, is the class attribute of the joined federate's known class for the object instance\linebreak
 containing the instance attribute that has the same attribute designator as the instance attribute.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{117.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{corresponding-instance-attributes-of-a-class-attribute}\HLADefinitionTerm{corresponding instance attributes of a class attribute}: The instance attributes that, from the perspective\linebreak
 of a given joined federate, are%
 }

 \HLAFixedAlphaList{100.02}{153.78}{421.98}{6}{%
 \item Unowned instance attributes of object instances that have a known class at the joined federate equal\linebreak
 to the object class of the class attribute and that have the same attribute designator as the class\linebreak
 attribute, or
 \item Instance attributes owned by the joined federate that belong to object instances that have a known\linebreak
 class at the owning federate equal to the object class of the class attribute and that have the same\linebreak
 attribute designator as the class attribute.
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{243.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{current-federation-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{current federation object model (FOM)}: The union of the FOM modules and one Management Object\linebreak
 Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM) that have been specified in the creation of the federation\linebreak
 execution or by any federate that has joined the federation execution. The sum operation is carried out\linebreak
 according to the rules as prescribed in IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025. When all FOM modules have been\linebreak
 provided, the current FOM will be equal to the FOM; and before this step has happened, the current FOM\linebreak
 will be a true subset of the FOM.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{327.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{current-federation-object-model-document-data}\HLADefinitionTerm{current federation object model (FOM) Document Data (FDD)}: The data and information used to\linebreak
 configure the federation execution that is the union of the FOM modules and one Management Object\linebreak
 Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM) that have been specified in the creation of the federation\linebreak
 execution or by any federate that has joined the federation execution. The sum operation is carried out\linebreak
 according to the rules as prescribed in IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025. When all FOM modules have been\linebreak
 provided, the current FDD will be equal to the FDD; and before this step has happened, the current FDD will\linebreak
 be a true subset of the FDD.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{423.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{data-type}\HLADefinitionTerm{data type}: A representation convention for a data element establishing its format, resolution, cardinality,\linebreak
 and ordinality.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{459.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{declared-attributes}\HLADefinitionTerm{declared attributes}: The set of class attributes of a particular object class that are listed in the federation\linebreak
 object model (FOM) as being associated with that object class in the object class hierarchy tree.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{495.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{declared-directed-interaction}\HLADefinitionTerm{declared directed interaction}: The set of class directed interactions of a particular object class that are\linebreak
 listed in the federation object model (FOM) as being associated with that object class in the object class\linebreak
 hierarchy tree.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{543.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{declared-parameters}\HLADefinitionTerm{declared parameters}: The set of parameters of a particular interaction class that are listed in the federation\linebreak
 object model (FOM) as being associated with that interaction class in the interaction class hierarchy tree.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{579.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{default-range}\HLADefinitionTerm{default range}: A range lower bound and a range upper bound, defined in the federation object model\linebreak
 (FOM) Document Data (FDD) and specified in terms of [0, the dimension's upper bound), for a dimension.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{615.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{default-region}\HLADefinitionTerm{default region}: A multidimensional region provided by the runtime infrastructure (RTI) that is composed of\linebreak
 one range for each dimension found in the federation object model (FOM) Document Data (FDD). The\linebreak
 bounds of each of these ranges are [0, the range's dimension's upper bound). There is no way for a federate\linebreak
 to refer to the default region.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{675.98}{NOTE---See 9.1.}
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{27}{26}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLADefinitionAt{69.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federate-application}\HLADefinitionTerm{federate application}: An application that supports the High Level Architecture (HLA) interface to a\linebreak
 runtime infrastructure (RTI) and that is capable of joining a federation execution. A federate application may\linebreak
 join the same federation execution multiple times or may join multiple federation executions. However, each\linebreak
 time a federate application joins a federation execution, it is creating a new joined federate. \emph{See also}: \textbf{joined}\linebreak
 \textbf{federate}.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{141.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation}: A named set of federate applications and a common federation object model (FOM) that are\linebreak
 used as a whole to achieve some specific objective.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{177.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-execution}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation execution}: The actual operation, over time, of a set of joined federates that are interconnected by\linebreak
 a runtime infrastructure (RTI).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{213.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-objectives}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation objectives}: The statement of the problem that is to be addressed by the establishment and\linebreak
 execution of a federation.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{249.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation object model (FOM)}: A specification defining the information exchanged at runtime to achieve\linebreak
 a given set of federation objectives. This information includes object classes, object class attributes,\linebreak
 interaction classes, interaction parameters, and other relevant information. The FOM is specified to the\linebreak
 runtime infrastructure (RTI) using one or more FOM modules. The RTI assembles a FOM using these FOM\linebreak
 modules and one Management Object Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM), which is provided\linebreak
 automatically by the RTI or, optionally, provided to the RTI when the federation execution is created.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{333.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-object-model-document-data}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation object model (FOM) Document Data (FDD)}: The data and information in a FOM that are used\linebreak
 by the \emph{Create Federation Execution} service and successive \emph{Join Federation Execution} service invocations to\linebreak
 configure the federation execution.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{381.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-object-model-module}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation object model (FOM) module}: A partial FOM (containing some or all object model template\linebreak
 (OMT) tables) that specifies a modular component of a FOM. A FOM module may contain classes not\linebreak
 inherent to it but upon which the FOM module depends, i.e., superclasses to the modular components. These\linebreak
 superclasses will be included in the FOM module as either complete or scaffolding definitions.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{441.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-requirements}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation requirements}: A statement that identifies a federation characteristic, constraint, process, or\linebreak
 product that is unambiguous and testable and that is necessary for a federation to be acceptable for its\linebreak
 intended use.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{489.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{federation-scenario}\HLADefinitionTerm{federation scenario}: A set of initial conditions and timeline of significant events used within a federation\linebreak
 execution to achieve federation objectives.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{525.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{final-time-value}\HLADefinitionTerm{final time value}: The point on the time axis for which no other points occurs after it.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{549.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{handle}\HLADefinitionTerm{handle}: An identifier originated/created by the runtime infrastructure (RTI) that is unique to a federation\linebreak
 execution.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{585.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{inherited-attribute}\HLADefinitionTerm{inherited attribute}: A class attribute of an object class that was declared in a superclass of that object class\linebreak
 in the object class hierarchy tree defined in the federation object model (FOM).%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{621.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{inherited-dimension}\HLADefinitionTerm{inherited dimension}:%
 }

 \HLAFixedAlphaList{100.02}{645.78}{421.98}{0}{%
 \item Pertaining to an object class: a dimension of an object class that was declared in a superclass of that\linebreak
 object class in the object class hierarchy tree defined in the federation object model (FOM) or\linebreak
 simulation object model (SOM).
 \item Pertaining to an interaction class: a dimension of an interaction class that was declared in a\linebreak
 superclass of that interaction class in the interaction class hierarchy tree defined in the federation\linebreak
 object model (FOM) or simulation object model (SOM).
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}

 \HLAFixedBlock{90}{69.79}{432}{\rmfamily}{9.96}{12}{%
 the object instance (however, the object instance is not to be eliminated and may be rediscovered). \emph{See also}:\linebreak
 \textbf{delete}.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{105.98}{NOTE---See 6.18.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{127.81}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{logical-time}\HLADefinitionTerm{logical time}: The representation of discrete points on the time axis. Logical time is used to represent a\linebreak
 federate's time position and the timestamps of messages.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{163.81}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{logical-time-interval}\HLADefinitionTerm{logical time interval}: The representation of the distance between two points on the time axis. Logical time\linebreak
 interval is used to represent a time-regulating federate's lookahead and by the RTI to perform arithmetic on\linebreak
 logical time values.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{211.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{lookahead}\HLADefinitionTerm{lookahead}: A logical time interval provided by joined federates that become time-regulating. When added\linebreak
 to the time-regulating joined federate's time position, the resulting timestamp is used to calculate the bound\linebreak
 on the timestamps that the time-regulating joined federate can use to send timestamp order (TSO) messages.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{259.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{lost-federate}\HLADefinitionTerm{lost federate}: A previously joined federate that, as a result of a fault, can no longer continue in the\linebreak
 federation execution in a High Level Architecture (HLA) compliant manner.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{295.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{management-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{Management Object Model (MOM)}: A group of predefined High Level Architecture (HLA) constructs\linebreak
 (object and interaction classes) that provide the following:%
 }

 \HLAFixedAlphaList{100.02}{331.80}{421.98}{0}{%
 \item Access to federation execution operating information
 \item Insight into the operations of joined federates and the runtime infrastructure (RTI)
 \item Control of the functioning of the RTI, the federation execution, and the individual joined federates
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{379.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{management-object-model-and-initialization-module}\HLADefinitionTerm{Management Object Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM)}: A subset of the federation object\linebreak
 model (FOM) that contains object model template (OMT) tables that describe the High Level Architecture\linebreak
 (HLA) MOM. The MIM also contains additional predefined HLA constructs such as object and interaction\linebreak
 roots, data types, transportation types, and dimensions. HLA specifies a standard MIM that is incorporated\linebreak
 into all FOM Document Data (FDD) automatically by the runtime infrastructure (RTI). The standard MIM\linebreak
 can be replaced with a user-supplied MIM containing the standard MIM plus extensions.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{463.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{message}\HLADefinitionTerm{message}: A change of object instance attribute value(s), an interaction, a directed interaction, or a deletion\linebreak
 of an existing object instance, often associated with a particular point on the time axis, as denoted by the\linebreak
 associated timestamp.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{511.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{null-designator}\HLADefinitionTerm{null designator}: A designator reserved to indicate an empty value that is distinguishable from all other\linebreak
 designators. A null designator is guaranteed to compare unequal to any other designator with a nonempty\linebreak
 value.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{559.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{object-class}\HLADefinitionTerm{object class}: A fundamental element of a conceptual representation for a federate that reflects the real world\linebreak
 at levels of abstraction and resolution appropriate for federate interoperability. An object class is a template\linebreak
 for a set of characteristics that is common to a group of object instances. These characteristics correspond to\linebreak
 the class attributes and class directed interactions that individual federates may publish and to which other\linebreak
 federates may subscribe.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{631.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{object-instance}\HLADefinitionTerm{object instance}: A unique instantiation of an object class that is independent of all other instances of that\linebreak
 object class. At any point during a federation execution, the state of a High Level Architecture (HLA) object\linebreak
 instance is defined as the collection of the values of all its instance attributes.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{679.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{object model}: A system specification defined primarily by class characteristics and relationships. The High\linebreak
 Level Architecture (HLA) idea of an object model is similar in many ways, but not identical, to the common\linebreak
 idea of an object model in object-oriented literature.%
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{33}{32}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLADefinitionAt{69.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{region-template}\HLADefinitionTerm{region template}: A region template is an incomplete region specification where one or more dimensions\linebreak
 have not been assigned ranges.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{105.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{register}\HLADefinitionTerm{register}: To invoke the \emph{Register Object Instance} or the \emph{Register Object Instance With Regions} service to\linebreak
 create a unique object instance designator.%
 }
 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{141.98}{NOTE---See 6.8.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{163.81}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{registered-class}\HLADefinitionTerm{registered class}: The object class that was an argument to the \emph{Register Object Instance} or the \emph{Register}\linebreak
 \emph{Object Instance With Regions} service invocation that resulted in the creation of the object instance\linebreak
 designator for a given object instance.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{211.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{regular-interaction-class-description}\HLADefinitionTerm{regular interaction class description}: A description of an interaction class that follows IEEE Std\linebreak
 1516.2\texttrademark-2025 and contains at a minimum the interaction class name and publish/subscribe indicator.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{247.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{regular-object-class-description}\HLADefinitionTerm{regular object class description}: A description of an object class that follows IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025 and\linebreak
 contains at a minimum the object class name and publish/subscribe indicator.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{283.80}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{remove}\HLADefinitionTerm{remove}: To receive an invocation of the \emph{Remove Object Instance \textdagger{}} service for a particular object instance.%
 }
 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{308.00}{NOTE---See 6.17.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{329.77}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{repeated-description}\HLADefinitionTerm{repeated description}: A description of a construct (e.g., object class, interaction class, data type,\linebreak
 dimension) in a federation object model (FOM) module with a name and additional properties that are\linebreak
 identical to a description that is already available in the current FOM.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{377.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{resolution}\HLADefinitionTerm{resolution}: The smallest resolvable value separating attribute or parameter values that can be discriminated.\linebreak
 Resolution may vary with magnitude for certain data types.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{413.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{retraction}\HLADefinitionTerm{retraction}: An action performed by a federate to unschedule a previously scheduled message. Message\linebreak
 retraction may be visible to the federate to whom the scheduled message was to be delivered. Retraction is\linebreak
 widely used in classic event-oriented discrete event simulations to model behaviors such as preemption and\linebreak
 interrupts.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{473.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{runtime-infrastructure}\HLADefinitionTerm{runtime infrastructure (RTI)}: The software that provides common interface services during a High Level\linebreak
 Architecture (HLA) federation execution for synchronization and data exchange.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{509.82}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{runtime-infrastructure-initialization-data}\HLADefinitionTerm{runtime infrastructure (RTI) initialization data (RID)}: RTI vendor-specific information needed to run an\linebreak
 RTI. If required, a RID is supplied when an RTI is initialized.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{545.82}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{scaffolding-interaction-class-description}\HLADefinitionTerm{scaffolding interaction class description}: A description of an interaction class in a federation object model\linebreak
 (FOM) module or simulation object model (SOM) module that follows IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025. However,\linebreak
 it will contain only the name. The name of the scaffolding interaction class description is identical to the\linebreak
 name of a regular interaction class description provided by another FOM/SOM module. Scaffolding\linebreak
 interaction class descriptions act as placeholders in order to represent the class hierarchy from the other\linebreak
 FOM/SOM module(s) from which a new regular interaction class description can be specified.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{629.82}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{scaffolding-object-class-description}\HLADefinitionTerm{scaffolding object class description}: A description of an object class in a federation object model (FOM)\linebreak
 module or simulation object model (SOM) module that follows IEEE Std 1516.2\texttrademark-2025. However, it will\linebreak
 contain only the name. The name of the scaffolding object class description is identical to the name of a\linebreak
 regular object class description provided by another FOM/SOM module. Scaffolding object class\linebreak
 descriptions act as placeholders in order to represent the class hierarchy from the other FOM/SOM\linebreak
 module(s) from which a new regular object class description can be specified.%
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
\clearpage

\HLASourcePage{34}{33}
\thispagestyle{hla-body}
\begin{hlafixedpage}
 \HLADefinitionAt{69.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{sent-class}\HLADefinitionTerm{sent class}: The interaction class that was an argument to the \emph{Send Interaction} or \emph{Send Interaction With}\linebreak
 \emph{Regions} service invocation that initiated the sending of a given interaction.%
 }
 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{105.98}{NOTE---See 5.1.3.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{127.81}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{sent-interaction}\HLADefinitionTerm{sent interaction}: A specific interaction that is transmitted by a joined federate via the \emph{Send Interaction},\linebreak
 \emph{Send Interaction With Regions}, or \emph{Send Directed Interaction} service and received by other joined federates\linebreak
 in the federation execution via the \emph{Receive Interaction \textdagger{}} or \emph{Receive Directed Interaction \textdagger{}} service.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{175.81}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{sent-parameters}\HLADefinitionTerm{sent parameters}: The parameters that were arguments to the \emph{Send Interaction}, \emph{Send Interaction With}\linebreak
 \emph{Regions}, or \emph{Send Directed Interaction} service invocation for a given interaction.%
 }
 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{209.00}{NOTE---See 5.1.3.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{230.77}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{set}\HLADefinitionTerm{set}: A group of elements in which each element occurs at most once (this definition corresponds to the\linebreak
 mathematical notion of sets). An example of a set would be a group of class attributes, each of which\linebreak
 belongs to the same object class.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{278.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{simulation-object-model}\HLADefinitionTerm{simulation object model (SOM)}: A specification of the types of information that an individual federate\linebreak
 could provide to High Level Architecture (HLA) federations as well as the information that an individual\linebreak
 federate can receive from other federates in HLA federations. The SOM is specified using one or more SOM\linebreak
 modules. The standard format in which SOMs are expressed facilitates determination of the suitability of\linebreak
 federates for participation in a federation.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{350.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{simulation-object-model-module}\HLADefinitionTerm{simulation object model (SOM) module}: A subset of the SOM that contains some or all object model\linebreak
 template (OMT) tables. SOM modules and one optional Management Object Model (MOM) and\linebreak
 Initialization Module (MIM) are used to specify the SOM of a federate. A SOM module contains complete\linebreak
 or scaffolding definitions for all object classes and interaction classes that are superclasses of object classes\linebreak
 and interaction classes in the same SOM module.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{422.76}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{specified-dimensions}\HLADefinitionTerm{specified dimensions}: The dimensions that are explicitly provided when the region specification is created\linebreak
 or modified.%
 }
 \HLADefinitionNoteAt{90}{455.96}{NOTE---See 9.1.2.}

 \HLADefinitionAt{477.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{stop-publishing}\HLADefinitionTerm{stop publishing}: To take action that results in a class attribute that had been a published attribute of a class\linebreak
 no longer being a published attribute of that class.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{513.79}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{subclass}\HLADefinitionTerm{subclass}: A class that adds additional detail to (specializes) another more generic class (superclass). A\linebreak
 subclass, by inheriting the properties from its parent class (closest superclass), also inherits the properties of\linebreak
 all superclasses of its parent as well.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{561.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{subscribe}\HLADefinitionTerm{subscribe}: To announce to a federation the information a federate wants from the federation.%
 }

 \HLADefinitionAt{585.78}{%
 \HLADefinitionAnchor{subscribed}\HLADefinitionTerm{subscribed}:%
 }

 \HLAFixedAlphaList{100.02}{607.80}{421.98}{0}{%
 \item Pertaining to an object class from the perspective of a given joined federate: having subscribed\linebreak
 attributes of that class or subscribed attributes of that class with regions, for some region. \emph{See also}:\linebreak
 \textbf{subscribed attributes of an object class}; \textbf{subscribed attributes of an object class with regions}.
 \item Pertaining to an interaction class: being a subscribed interaction class or a subscribed interaction\linebreak
 class with regions, for some region. \emph{See also}: \textbf{subscribed interaction class}; \textbf{subscribed interaction}\linebreak
 \textbf{class with regions}.
 }
\end{hlafixedpage}
